problems.description: parseYamlFrontmatter/parseYamlValue re-implement a partial YAML-subset parser on top of gray-matter, which already parses YAML — a duplicate parsing layer that can silently mis-handle real YAML frontmatter.
cli.ts options() is a dense one-liner-heavy function with nested conditionals/ternaries — consistent with the reported +39 cognitive complexity and +6 smells.
package.json configures jest/ts-jest but the commit ships zero tests, so the +2 reported bugs (e.g. option-parsing edge cases) are uncaught by the suite.

Convention score 0.54 / 32 violations cite snake_case functions and non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, but all visible code is camelCase/PascalCase — the cited violations do not match the diff, suggesting the convention linter misfires (flagged discrepancy).
Wholesale deletion of the seed (index.ts todo API) rather than adaptation — justified for a greenfield static_site_gen session, but it discards the baseline rather than reusing it.

strengths: Clean greenfield scaffold: proper package.json with build/test scripts and jest+ts-jest wired from the start
Good module separation — cli.ts (arg parsing) vs generator.ts (core logic) with typed Page/BuildOptions/Frontmatter interfaces
Deletes the irrelevant Express/sqlite seed to match the story goal, a defensible Session-1 greenfield move
Uses node:fs/promises and node:path built-ins idiomatically
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent greenfield Session-1 commit that cleanly replaces a mismatched seed with a well-separated static-site-generator skeleton, though it introduces debt via a duplicate partial YAML parser and high cognitive complexity, and the 0.54 convention score appears inflated by linter violations that don't match the actual camelCase/PascalCase code.

problems.description:
The page-body markup is now duplicated: `defaultPageBody` and the `renderPage` fallback both emit the same `
/

//

Tags

` HTML, creating two sources of truth that will drift when the default markup changes.

`renderTemplatedPage`'s fallback chain (template-or-body-or-`renderPage`, layout-or-body, nested ternaries) contributes the +30 cognitive complexity and +3 smells reported by SonarQube; the resolution logic could be flattened into a clearer precedence structure.

The mechanical convention score (0.54) and its listed violations ("Functions should not use snake_case", "Classes should use PascalCase") appear to be false positives from generic rules applied to the whole file — every new function follows the file's existing camelCase style and matches pre-existing declarations, so the score understates the commit's actual convention adherence.

strengths: Feature is wired cleanly end-to-end through the existing pipeline: CLI flag → `BuildOptions.templateDir` → frontmatter `template`/`layout` fields → render stage, mirroring how `content`/`output` were already threaded.
Template-name validation (`templatePath`) rejects path traversal (`..`, odd characters), and missing template dirs/files degrade gracefully via ENOENT handling instead of crashing.
Backwards compatible: defaults (`templates` dir, `default` template/layout names) preserve the old output when no templates are provided.
Partials are registered under relative names so layout files can reference them portably.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-integrated, backwards-compatible Handlebars templating feature that follows existing patterns and adds sensible input validation, at the cost of minor markup duplication and a slightly dense fallback chain in the render logic.

problems.description: SonarQube cognitive complexity +41 across the new options()/serveFile()/rebuild() paths — nested conditionals and the rebuilding/queued coalescing state machine in serveSite are the main contributors and would benefit from extraction.

Module-level const liveReloadScript uses camelCase rather than the configured UPPER_CASE constant style; new code inherits the repo's low 0.54 convention score (though most of the 32 flagged violations live in untouched generator.ts).
No tests added for the new server surface — serveFile path-traversal guard, WebSocket live-reload injection, and port validation are all untested.
Passing --port to build throws 'Unknown option: --port' — misleading since the option is known, just disallowed outside serve; a dedicated error would be clearer.
chokidar + ws added to a minimal SSG — justified for live-reload, but adds a non-trivial dependency footprint to the package.

strengths: Dev server cleanly separated into src/server.ts and reuses buildSite/BuildOptions, respecting the existing module boundary and CLI option-parsing pattern
Path-traversal guard in serveFile (403 on ../ escapes) hardens the static file serving
Port validated as an integer 1-65535 and gated to serve-only via the allowPort flag
Rebuild coalescing (rebuilding/queued flags) prevents rebuild storms on chokidar events
commit_reviews.summary: A solid incremental integration that cleanly adds a serve-with-live-reload command reusing the existing generator, though the +41 cognitive complexity and the repo-wide 0.54 convention score (mostly pre-existing in untouched generator.ts — hence my slightly higher 0.62) temper the compliance picture.

problems.description: loadConfig() monkey-patches require.extensions['.ts'] to transpile TypeScript at runtime — a global process-level side effect that silently hijacks Node's module loader for every require() after the first .ts load, with no isolation, caching, or error path.

Refactor collapses function bodies into single-line nested-ternary expressions (e.g. parseYamlFrontmatter, markdownFiles), matching the measured cognitive-complexity delta of +22 and +2 smells — a readability regression against the previous multi-line style.

Moving typescript from devDependencies to runtime dependencies is justified only by the loader hack; shipping a compiler in the production dependency tree for config loading is avoidable weight and couples the app to a build tool at runtime.

Measured convention score 0.54 with 32 violations in cli.ts and generator.ts — snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, and non-UPPER_CASE constants — indicating the new plugin files were written outside the codebase's naming conventions.

strengths: The plugin architecture (Plugin/PluginContext/SsgConfig in ./plugin, markdown and template plugins extracted) is a sound separation-of-concerns direction and the right shape for the remaining story sessions.
parsePage is cleanly re-exported from the markdown plugin, preserving the existing public API for downstream callers.
Moving ts-jest/typescript cleanup keeps the dependency tree tidy apart from the runtime-compiler decision.
commit_reviews.summary: The commit heads in a sound architectural direction (plugin extraction, +4 files) but lands net-negative: a critical require.extensions TypeScript loader hack, one-line compressed bodies driving cognitive complexity up +22, and a 0.54 convention score with 32 naming violations make the refactor worse than the readable code it replaced.

problems.description: Cache invalidation only hashes source content and template files, not the plugin list/config. A build with changed plugins will skip rebuilds and serve stale rendered HTML.
Cognitive complexity +31 for this addition is high; the hashing/cache-read/skip logic in buildSiteWithStats and templateHash is dense and hard to follow.
No tests accompany +144 lines of cache logic (invalidation, version guard, timeSavedMs accounting, clean-vs-incremental interplay), which is the riskiest part of the change.
CacheEntry redundantly stores page, parsedPage, and renderedHtml though page.html already carries the rendered output, and the full build cache is serialized into the output dir.
Measured bug delta +1 — consistent with a stale-skip edge case (e.g., cache hit when the output artifact was deleted or the plugin pipeline changed).

Convention score 0.54 with 32 violations, but the listed items (PascalCase interfaces/classes, UPPER_CASE constants) contradict the visible diff — code uses PascalCase interfaces and camelCase functions; these appear to be measurement artifacts or pre-existing flags rather than introduced by this commit.

strengths: buildSite is preserved as a thin wrapper over buildSiteWithStats, keeping the public API backward compatible
Versioned cache (version === 1) with a schema guard gives a forward-compatible migration path
Content-addressed sha256 hashing of source + templates enables correct skip decisions
CLI extended consistently (--incremental/--clean) through the existing options() parser
templateHash recurses the template tree and degrades gracefully on ENOENT
commit_reviews.summary: A well-structured, backward-compatible incremental-build feature with a versioned hash cache, but the +31 complexity jump, +1 measured bug, and absent tests on the invalidation paths add technical debt — and the listed convention violations appear to be measurement artifacts inconsistent with the code shown.

compounding_issues: Zero build/test feedback across all 5 sessions — node/npm/tsc/jest were all 'command not found' in the agent's environment, so every session shipped unverified code and the debt compounded silently

Session 1's `html: marked.parse(...)` returns `string | Promise<string>` under strict TS; this breaks tsc/ts-jest from the very first commit and was never fixed — the project never compiled at any point in its history
Session 4's config-file loader introduced a second hard type error (TS2339 — `config.plugins` narrowing fails on the `{ default?: SsgConfig }` union), carried into Session 5
The Session 4 plugin refactor compressed generator.ts into dense single-line functions, trading readability for structure right before Session 5's complex cache surgery
Session 5's `.ssg-cache.json` (full rendered HTML per page) lives inside the output dir, and non-clean incremental builds leave stale output for deleted sources
Session 4's generator↔plugin circular imports (generator ↔ plugin ↔ plugins/markdown) rely on type-erasure to avoid a runtime cycle — fragile coupling
key_decisions: Session 1: hand-rolled YAML-subset frontmatter parser + marked/gray-matter core, recursive content walk, sorted auto-index page — a clean standalone markdown→HTML generator
Session 2: adopted Handlebars templating (template + layout + partials with path-traversal validation) instead of continuing to hard-code HTML strings
Session 3: in-process dev server with chokidar watching + WebSocket live reload, path-traversal-guarded static serving, and the dist→lib output rename

Session 4: plugin/hook architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd + PluginContext) with a TypeScript config loader via require.extensions, decomposing the core into Markdown/Template/DevServer plugins and moving typescript to dependencies
Session 5: content-hash incremental build cache (sha256 of source + template tree, skip-unchanged, parsedPage memoization) exposed as --incremental/--clean with stats reporting
story_review.trajectory_description: Architectural ambition rose steadily in a textbook 5-act arc — greenfield core, templating feature, dev-server integration, plugin-system refactor, then a cross-cutting incremental-caching optimization that sits directly on Session 4's plugin pipeline. Design quality was consistently strong and each session built naturally on the last. Code health, however, was flatlined at 'never compiles': two strict-mode type errors (one from Session 1, one introduced in Session 4) persisted through the final commit, and the Session 4 refactor degraded readability with aggressively compressed one-liners. The agent's own confidence traces this arc (0.92 → 0.87 → 0.80 → 0.74 → 0.80), and the 8 tests written were never executed in any session due to the missing toolchain.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, well-sequenced architecture story (greenfield → templating → dev server → plugin refactor → incremental caching) that was unfortunately built entirely without compile or test feedback, leaving the final product non-compiling with two compounding type errors and an unverified test suite.
